rv.q: I can't overstate how glad I am that I went.
"Bill W. and Dr. Bob” is about the possibilities of personal transformation, but in this production the characters’ inner journeys feel flat.
The play by Samuel Shem and Janet Surrey brings these stories to vibrant life, unfiltered from the official recovery version.
Despite its clear appeal for “friends of Bill and Bob,” the script needs improvement in story clarity and the staging needs more creativity in production values.
It’s an engaging, heartwarming, gently humorous story with a real message: sobriety must be built on a community of same genre suffering.
This is a solid cast, making each of the snippets that tell this powerful story work This is not a show for everyone.

cn.t: Critics find this account of AA's founding moving and historically compelling, though some note the play's straightforward storytelling lacks dramatic complexity. The inspiring subject matter resonates more than the theatrical execution.
